# clawsweeper-review — the review half of PR validation

## The contract

`clawsweeper-review` runs ONE review of the tree mounted at `/target` against the base ref in
`BASE_SHA`, and prints the engine's JSON to stdout. It is **advisory**: it never gates a merge,
never writes to GitHub, and is given no token.

```bash
docker run --rm --read-only \
  -e OLLAMA_API_KEY -e CLAWSWEEPER_TARGET_REPO -e BASE_SHA \
  -v "$PWD:/target:ro" \
  ghcr.io/opencharly/clawsweeper-review:<calver>
```

`--local-range` is the only mode this image offers. It reviews `merge-base(base, HEAD)..HEAD`,
refuses a dirty tree, and makes no GitHub reads or writes — which is what lets it run with the
PR tree mounted read-only and no credential.

## The pins and why each one exists

| Pin | Value source | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAWSWEEPER_COMMIT` | this candy's `var:` | the engine and its prompt/schema would float |
| `NODE_VERSION` | `24.x` | the engine requires Node >= 24 |
| `PNPM_VERSION` | `12.4.1` | the lockfile is frozen against it |
| `CODEX_VERSION` | `0.162.1` | Codex is the engine's only runner; a different version changes the wire contract |

## The model path (measured)

Codex accepts **only** `wire_api = "responses"`. Ollama Cloud serves stateless Responses at
`https://ollama.com/v1`, so the image writes:

```toml
model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"
model_provider = "ollama-cloud"
[model_providers.ollama-cloud]
base_url = "https://ollama.com/v1"
env_key = "OLLAMA_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = false
```

Proven with a tool call, not a completion: `codex exec` was asked to run `uname -s && uname -m`
and returned `Linux` / `x86_64` from inside its sandbox. If a future Codex or endpoint change
contradicts this, re-run that probe before touching the candy.

## The target profile

ClawSweeper refuses a repository it has no profile for. The candy appends a **generic fallback
for owner `opencharly`**, so any `opencharly/<repo>` resolves without a per-repo entry and an
upstream sync never conflicts with a local config edit. The candy asserts the entry exists.

## Sandbox prerequisites

Codex's read-only review sandbox uses bubblewrap, which needs unprivileged user namespaces. The
runner image (`github-runner-ubuntu`) sets
`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` and `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1`; a host
without those fails at browser-free sandbox setup, not in this engine.

## Failure classes, kept distinct

- **Engine produced a verdict** → the caller posts it.
- **Provider never answered / empty completion** → no verdict; the caller reports it as
  inconclusive and stays advisory.
- **A missing tool in the image** → the build-time `check:` steps name it (`node`, `pnpm`,
  `codex`, the engine's `--help`, the profile, the config, the entrypoint).
